meta.title: Auto Insurance Decline Rule Submissions — AI-Assisted Regulatory Review
meta.description: 100 fictionalized insurer decline-rule submissions with pre-computed, corpus-grounded regulatory assessments, recommendations, and draft insurer responses. The AI recommendation is a fixed record of what the tool advised; a human reviewer records the final decision, may edit the draft response, and owns every outcome.
meta.status_note: All submissions have completed AI assessment (baseline status 'AI reviewed'); a subset are seeded at later workflow stages to illustrate a review queue in operation. These seeded statuses are illustrative, not actual review history.
meta.grounding_note: All assessments are grounded solely in the legislation, regulations, and FSRA guidance contained in decline_rule_knowledge_base_34_FINAL.json. This is a decision-support prototype, not a regulatory decision.

submissions.rule_text: Decline to insure any applicant with 3 or more at-fault accidents in the preceding 3 years.
submissions.rationale: Historical claims data demonstrates a strong correlation between multiple at-fault accidents and future claims frequency. This threshold reflects an unacceptable level of demonstrated risk.
submissions.regulatory_analysis: The rule rests on at-fault accident history, an objective and risk-relevant ground. Under FSCO Bulletin A-1/01 an underwriting rule is acceptable where it is not subjective or arbitrary, bears a direct relationship to the potential risk, and is not contrary to public policy. At-fault accident history is not among the prohibited considerations in Reg. 664, s. 5(2), and s. 5(2.2) expressly permits considering an at-fault accident where, within the preceding three years, there was more than one and the driver was at fault.

citations.version: consolidated to June 26, 2025 (last amendment O. Reg. 56/25)

submissions.recommendation: The rule rests on an objective, risk-relevant ground that is not prohibited by the cited authorities. Insurer cites historical claims data but has not provided it; supporting actuarial data may be requested before sign-off. Final decision rests with the human reviewer.

submissions.rule_text: Decline to insure any applicant who does not own the vehicle listed on the policy.
submissions.rationale: Non-ownership creates ambiguity around insurable interest and increases the likelihood of moral hazard and fraudulent claims.
submissions.regulatory_analysis: Insurable interest/ownership is a legitimate underwriting concern, but a blanket decline for not owning the listed vehicle may capture common legitimate arrangements (leased, family, company vehicles). A-1/01 requires a direct relationship to risk and non-arbitrariness; the rule's breadth requires review.
submissions.recommendation: The cited authorities do not prohibit the rule outright, but they raise conditions or concerns that require the reviewer's judgment before the rule can be approved or refused. Reviewer should determine whether the concern is genuine insurable interest (addressable by other means) versus an arbitrary ownership requirement. Final decision rests with the human reviewer.

submissions.rule_text: Decline to insure any applicant whose primary language is not English or French.
submissions.rationale: Communication barriers may result in inaccurate policy information and increased disputes. Ensuring clear communication protects both the insurer and the consumer.
submissions.regulatory_analysis: The rule declines on the basis of language. A-1/01 prohibits grounds transgressing the Human Rights Code (nationality/ethnicity) and 'surrogates for them'; primary language is a surrogate for ethnic origin and place of origin. UDAP s. 4(1) independently prohibits unfair discrimination including Human Rights Code contraventions.

citations.source: Unfair or Deceptive Acts or Practices (UDAP) Rule, s. 4(1)
